description: Novation Nocturn control numbers. This is the source-of-truth table shared by the nuts driver (src/Nuts.Driver/appsettings.json, sections Midi:Mapping and Midi:Paging) and the Reason Remote codec (remote/Codecs/Lua Codecs/Nuts/Nocturn.lua, lookup tables at the top). Change all three together, then run remote/scripts/verify-map.ps1.

paging.description: The driver banks the CCs for the 8 dials and the 8 page-row buttons. A page is a set of parameters on those same physical controls. The four page SLOTS are generic: what a slot means is decided by the focused device's scope in remote/Maps/Nuts/Nocturn.remotemap (for the mixer channel: Mixer, Dynamics, EQ, FX). The driver steps the page from the PermaBar and echoes the live page to the codec on CC 119; the page buttons are consumed driver-side and never reach Reason. Only the dials and the page row bank - see 'shared' below.
paging.jumpButtons: surface index 15 = Mixer, 12 = Dynamics, 14 = EQ, 13 = FX (page order defines the -/+ wrap)
paging.budget: 40 shared + 64 banked = 104 of CC 0-119 used. 16 spare: 10-15, 42-47, 98-101.

ringModesPerPage.description: Ring display mode per dial, per page. Owned by the driver (Midi:Paging:RingModes); it repaints the modes on every page change. 0 = fill from minimum, 3 = centre both directions.
ringModesPerPage.note: Page 3 uses centre mode on the two bipolar gain dials (E1 HF Gain, E5 HMF Gain).

dials.description: Endless encoders, banked by page. Relative, two's complement: 1-63 = clockwise, 65-127 = counter-clockwise.
dials.rotation: see paging.dialCcs - CCs differ per page
dials.touchValues: 127 = touched, 0 = released. Reserved for soft takeover.

switches.description: The 16 buttons, modelled as switches, on CCs (not notes) in both directions: a CC carries an absolute value and keeps the whole note range on the loopback free for a keyboard. The hardware addresses these buttons and their LEDs by note number 0-15 on its USB wire; the driver re-publishes them as the CCs below and translates the LED CCs back. Each group has a kind (see docs/midi-mapping.md): "momentary" = press sends 127, release sends 0, the DAW owns the state and the LED; "toggle" = the driver keeps a latch, a press flips it, lights the LED and sends the new state (127 = on, 0 = off), a release is silent, and DAW feedback overwrites the latch. Measured on Reason 10 (2026-10-19): a codec "button" item acts on the press edge only and ignores a value 0, so a latching switch on a button item would toggle only every second press. The page row's codec items are therefore input="value" (absolute 0-127): Reason sets the Toggle remotables (Mute, Comp On, EQ On, ...) from the value, which is what makes toggle work end to end. Page row = toggle + value items; PermaBar = momentary + button items.

pageRow.description: 8 switches above the dials, green LEDs. Indices 0-7. Banked by page (see paging.pageRowCcs). Kind: toggle, and the codec declares one value item per page ('Button n P<n>').
pageRow.ccs: see paging.pageRowCcs - CCs differ per page; page 1 is 102-109

permaBar.description: 8 switches along the bottom, red LEDs. Indices 8-15 in surface order. Kind: momentary. The driver consumes all eight for paging - Page -/+ step the page, and MIXER/USER/INSTR/FX jump to one - so none of them reach Reason.

speedDial.description: Shared across pages - not banked. Relative, same encoding as the dials. The click is the only press on the speed dial.
speedDial.clickKind: momentary - a click, not a switch

crossfader.description: Shared across pages - not banked. 14-bit absolute pair [MSB, LSB]. The codec uses the MSB only (128 positions). Mapped to Pan on every page.

shared.description: Controls with one CC across every page. Everything not listed in paging.dialCcs / paging.pageRowCcs is shared.
shared.ccs: 24 speed dial, 118 speed dial click, 88 speed dial touch, 8/9 crossfader, 89 crossfader touch, 32-39 + 40 ring values, 48-55 ring modes, 110-117 PermaBar

feedbackToSurface.description: DAW -> surface. Knob ring values are 0-11 segments (the driver clamps anything higher); ring modes are 0-5; switch LEDs are on/off on the same CCs as the switches (0 = off, > 0 = on), which the driver turns into the hardware's note LED addresses. Rings do NOT bank: all four pages' knobs share the 8 ring CCs, and only the current page's item is ever moved. The driver holds one ring cache, so a page change blanks the rings until the new page repaints.
feedbackToSurface.switchLeds: same CCs as the switch table above (page 1: 102-109, page 2: 64-71, page 3: 90-97, page 4: 25-31 + 41). The driver resolves an incoming LED CC against the active page only, so inactive pages are ignored.

ringModes.description: Firmware-defined ring display modes. Per page; see paging.ringModesPerPage. gRingModes in Nocturn.lua is only the placeholder used before the driver's first page echo arrives.
ringModes.0: fill from minimum - used by the FX send levels and the non-bipolar dials
ringModes.3: centre, both directions - used by the EQ page's bipolar gains (E1 HF Gain, E5 HMF Gain)

pageParameters.description: What each page slot's 8 dials and 8 page-row buttons are mapped to, for the Reason Main Mixer Channel scope. Documentation only - the authority is remote/Maps/Nuts/Nocturn.remotemap, and verify-map.ps1 keeps the three contracts in step. The rule the layout follows: CONTINUOUS parameters live on dials, ON/OFF states live on the page-row switches. A value parameter on a toggle switch can only ever slam between 0 and 127. The map's item names are generic ('Knob n P<n>' / 'Button n P<n>'), where P1..P4 are the driver's page slots; this table names them by the mixer scope's page names instead. Every other scope in the map fills the same four slots with its own pages - see pages/*.yaml.

1 Mixer.note: Odd dials only - the gap separates the two filter groups from the input pair. B8 spare.

2 Dynamics.note: ALL 8 dials used - the page has 8 continuous parameters, so the odd/even gap is not kept. Top row E1-E4 is the compressor, bottom row E5-E8 the gate. Expander is a switch on B4. B7/B8 spare: 'Filters Dyn S/C' is already used on page 1, and a target may only be mapped once per scope.

3 EQ.note: Odd dials only, as page 1. E1 and E5 are the bipolar gains and use the centre ring mode.

4 FX.note: ALL 8 dials used: E1-E4 the insert rotaries, E5-E8 the send levels.
